module: Identify actors and design interaction disclosure

lesson.title: Make the interaction disclosure work: case exercise
lesson.summary: Make disclosure clear, timely and accessible in an agent-hotline case.

prerequisites.reason: The learner must identify a direct human interaction before testing this disclosure rule. The case requires a contextual decision on whether AI interaction is already obvious. The case requires the public-reporting carve-back and authorisation safeguards.
The case includes authorisation and reporting to the instructing person.

blocks: **Clear and distinguishable disclosure** enables the person to recognise the relevant AI involvement. Article 50(5) sets a latest point: first interaction or exposure.
A notice hidden in terms that appears after a conversation does not reliably inform the person at the required moment. Use plain wording near the relevant interaction.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 50(1), 50(5); Guidelines paragraphs 31, 137-144
Commission Article 50 Guidelines C(2026) 5054 final; non-binding interpretation
Final Transparency Code, 10 June 2026; voluntary implementation framework

blocks: **Accessible disclosure** conforms to the accessibility requirements applicable to the product, service or content. The Commission explains that Article 50 does not invent a separate universal accessibility regime.
Check which accessibility rules apply, then design information the audience can perceive and understand. A visual badge alone is unsuitable as the only notification in an audio-only interaction.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 50(1), 50(5); Guidelines paragraphs 31, 137-144
Commission Article 50 Guidelines C(2026) 5054 final; non-binding interpretation
Final Transparency Code, 10 June 2026; voluntary implementation framework

blocks: Account for intended or reasonably likely vulnerable audiences, such as children and people with disabilities. Guidance recommends understandable, age-appropriate information where children may interact.

The Code supplies practical approaches such as audible notices, screen-reader-compatible labels and sufficient contrast. These examples do not make one icon or technology a universal statutory requirement.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 50(1), 50(5); Guidelines paragraphs 31, 137-144
Commission Article 50 Guidelines C(2026) 5054 final; non-binding interpretation
Final Transparency Code, 10 June 2026; voluntary implementation framework

blocks: Case: Harbour provides a public offence-reporting AI hotline. Assume legal authorisation and safeguards are established. The service sounds like a human staff member and starts recording the report before giving an AI notice.

Public reporting retains the interaction duty. The human-like context does not establish obviousness. Move a clear notification to the start of interaction rather than relying on the end-of-call notice.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 50(1), 50(5); Guidelines paragraphs 31, 137-144
Commission Article 50 Guidelines C(2026) 5054 final; non-binding interpretation
Final Transparency Code, 10 June 2026; voluntary implementation framework

blocks: The hotline's agent acts for Harbour and later seeks approval from a supervising person. Use the principal and supervisory disclosures described by paragraph 31 of the Guidelines.

Provide a perceivable disclosure in the actual channel and the applicable accessible format. A logo in a web page is insufficient for a caller who only hears audio; another format may also be needed for people unable to hear it.

questions.prompt: Harbour gives its AI notice only after collecting a caller's offence report. What correction addresses Article 50(5)?

options.blocks: At the latest when interaction first begins
options.reason: The statutory latest point is first interaction or exposure.

options.blocks: Only after the caller's report is validated
options.reason: That is too late for the initial interaction.

options.blocks: Only when the caller opens a terms page
options.reason: Required information cannot depend on a delayed separate action.

questions.prompt: The hotline uses a visual AI badge, but callers interact only through audio. What must Harbour consider?

options.blocks: A larger badge on an unrelated page
options.reason: It remains unavailable in the actual audio interaction.

options.blocks: One mandatory icon that overrides accessibility law
options.reason: The Act requires applicable accessibility; it does not prescribe that universal icon.

options.blocks: A perceivable notice in the channel and applicable accessible formats
options.reason: Disclosure must work for the people and channel concerned.

questions.prompt: The authorised hotline is public-facing, sounds human and uses an agent representing Harbour. Which design is supported?

options.blocks: An end-of-call notice with no represented principal
options.reason: The timing is late and the agent guidance remains relevant.

options.blocks: A clear opening AI notice, represented-principal information and supervisor-step disclosure
options.reason: The carve-back, timing and agent guidance operate together.

options.blocks: No notice because legal authorisation overrides public reporting
options.reason: Public offence reporting retains the interaction duty.
